hints: Start from ammonia and ask what changes when its lone pair is used to bond to an extra $\text{H}^+$.
Count the bonding pairs and lone pairs around N in $\text{NH}_4^+$, this tells you the shape and the true H-N-H angle.
Remember a dative bond is identical once formed, then ask if $\text{NH}_4^+$ can donate a proton to $\text{OH}^-$.
walkthrough:
**How ammonium forms**

Think of ammonia using its lone pair to grab a proton. It is a friendly donation, not a different type of glue.

$$\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{NH}_4^+$$

**Find the shape and bond angle**

In $\text{NH}_3$ there are 3 bond pairs plus 1 lone pair, so pyramidal with about $107^\circ$. In $\text{NH}_4^+$ there are 4 bond pairs and 0 lone pairs.

$$\text{4 bond pairs, 0 lone pairs = tetrahedral = } 109.5^\circ$$

**Are the bonds different?**

One N-H bond started as dative covalent, but once formed all four N-H bonds are identical in length and strength. Electrons are shared the same way.

$$\text{dative covalent = covalent once formed}$$

**Is ammonium an acid?**

Yes, $\text{NH}_4^+$ can donate a proton back to become $\text{NH}_3$. It is the conjugate acid of a weak base, so it acts as a weak acid and reacts with strong bases.

$$\text{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

options.A: Incorrect. $90^\circ$ is the angle in octahedral shapes with 6 bond pairs. $\text{NH}_4^+$ has only 4 bond pairs and is tetrahedral with $109.5^\circ$.
options.B: Incorrect. $107^\circ$ is the H-N-H angle in $\text{NH}_3$, where the lone pair squeezes the bonds together. In $\text{NH}_4^+$ the lone pair is gone, so repulsion is equal and the angle opens to $109.5^\circ$.
options.C: Incorrect. This is the classic dative bond trap. The method of formation is different, but once the N-H dative bond is formed it is identical in strength and length to the other three N-H bonds.
options.D: Correct. $\text{NH}_4^+$ is the conjugate acid of the weak base $\text{NH}_3$. It can donate a proton, so it behaves as a weak acid and reacts with a base like $\text{OH}^-$ to form $\text{NH}_3$ and water.
